title: The History of Metal Gear | From MSX2 to Snake Eater Delta | Gaming History
description: The full history of Konami's Metal Gear series: Hideo Kojima's original in 1987, Metal Gear Solid, Snake Eater, The Phantom Pain, the Master Collection and the Snake Eater remake.

sections.heading: Tactical espionage action
sections.script: A cardboard box that moves by itself, a soldier who whispers over a radio, and a giant walking tank hiding in the dark. Metal Gear is one of the most influential series in gaming, and it helped invent the stealth genre. For nearly forty years it has mixed sneaking, cinematic storytelling and big ideas about war, technology and identity. In this video we follow the full history: the first game on the MSX2 in nineteen eighty seven, the PlayStation breakthrough with Metal Gear Solid in nineteen ninety eight, the golden years of Snake Eater and Guns of the Patriots, the Phantom Pain, and the return of Snake Eater in twenty twenty five. Keep your eyes open, and do not get spotted.

sections.heading: The first Metal Gear
sections.script: The story begins in nineteen eighty seven with a young designer at Konami named Hideo Kojima. His first Metal Gear game came out for the MSX2 computer in Japan and Europe. Kojima had planned an action game full of gunfights, but the hardware could not show many bullets or enemies on the screen. So he changed the idea and built the game around hiding and escaping, inspired by the film The Great Escape. You play Solid Snake, a rookie of the unit FOXHOUND, who infiltrates the fortress of Outer Heaven to destroy a walking weapon called Metal Gear. A different team made a heavily changed version for the Nintendo Entertainment System later that year, which is how many players in the West first met Snake.

sections.heading: Metal Gear 2 Solid Snake
sections.script: Konami also made an NES sequel called Snake's Revenge, but Kojima was not part of it. One of that game's designers met him and asked him to make a real sequel. Kojima agreed and created Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake, released in nineteen ninety on the MSX2 in Japan. It carried on the story of Solid Snake and deepened the themes of the first game, with ideas about the Cold War, politics and the cost of weapons. Metal Gear 2 was a big step for the series, and it set up the dramatic ideas that the next entries would explore. It would take until the PlayStation era for the series to reach a global audience, and many Western players only discovered this game much later, through modern collections of the early titles.

sections.heading: Metal Gear Solid
sections.script: Everything changed with the PlayStation. Kojima began work on his third Metal Gear game in nineteen ninety four, showed it at the Tokyo Game Show in nineteen ninety six, and released Metal Gear Solid in Japan on September third, nineteen ninety eight. It moved the series into three dimensional graphics, with voice acting, cutscenes directed like a film, and a story full of twists. The series became known for cinematic video games, a name that critics still use today. Solid Snake infiltrates a nuclear weapons disposal facility in Alaska, faces his twin brother Liquid Snake, and destroys Metal Gear REX. The game was a hit around the world and sold more than six million copies. It gave the series international fame and turned Snake into a gaming icon.

sections.heading: Sons of Liberty
sections.script: In November of two thousand one, Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty arrived on the PlayStation 2. The trailers had shown Snake, but the game surprised everyone by making you play mostly as a new hero, a rookie called Raiden. The story, set on a huge offshore facility called the Big Shell, dealt with controlled information, memes and who we really are, years before social media took over our lives. Many players were confused at the time, and the game is now praised as one of the most daring sequels ever made. A remake of the first game, Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes, followed a few years later. The series had become a giant, and the story was only getting bigger.

sections.heading: Snake Eater
sections.script: Then the series went back in time. Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater launched in two thousand four on the PlayStation 2, set during the Cold War. You play Naked Snake, an agent in the jungles of the Soviet Union, on a mission that is tied to his mentor, The Boss. The game added survival ideas to the stealth formula, and it is a prequel that explains how Big Boss became a legend. Many fans and critics call it the best Metal Gear of all, and its sad, emotional ending is still discussed today. In two thousand eight, Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots on the PlayStation 3 closed the story of an aging Solid Snake, with a huge finale.

sections.heading: Peace Walker and Rising
sections.script: After the main story ended, the series kept growing. Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker arrived in April of twenty ten on the PlayStation Portable, bringing a huge base building system where you recruit soldiers for your private army. It is set ten years after Snake Eater and follows the young Big Boss. In twenty thirteen came Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance on the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, a fast sword action spin off starring the cyborg ninja Raiden. It was a very different style, but fans loved its speed and slicing combat. The two games showed that the series could grow beyond pure stealth, and each one found a loyal audience of its own.

sections.heading: The Phantom Pain
sections.script: The biggest chapter of the last decade was Metal Gear Solid Five. The prologue, Ground Zeroes, came first, followed by the full game, The Phantom Pain, on September first, twenty fifteen. It put Big Boss in a large open world and let players choose how to approach every mission, with a mother base that players build and grow. Kiefer Sutherland replaced David Hayter as the voice of Snake. The gameplay is often named among the best in the series. But the release also marked the end of an era. Hideo Kojima left Konami in twenty fifteen, and later started his own studio. Konami continued the series without him, and for years the future looked uncertain.

sections.heading: Collections and a return
sections.script: For years, Metal Gear stayed quiet, but fans never let it die. In twenty twenty three, Konami announced two big projects at the PlayStation Showcase in May. One was the Metal Gear Solid Master Collection, whose first volume released later in twenty twenty three, bundling the first five main Metal Gear games, from the MSX2 originals to Snake Eater. The other was a full remake of Snake Eater. Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater launched on August twenty eighth, twenty twenty five, for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series consoles and PC. Konami said it passed one million copies on launch day, and later reported over two million by March of twenty twenty six. Volume Two, with Guns of the Patriots on new platforms, arrived on August twenty seventh, twenty twenty six.

sections.heading: Legacy and your say
sections.script: Konami now says the Metal Gear series has sold more than sixty million copies worldwide, a huge number for a stealth series. It popularized the stealth genre, helped create the idea of the cinematic video game, and left a legacy that influenced countless developers. From a limited MSX2 game to a PlayStation hit, to a remake in twenty twenty five, the history of Metal Gear shows how one idea can grow. We want to hear from you. Which Metal Gear is your favorite, and would you like to see a remake of Metal Gear Solid One or Two next? Do you prefer the stealth of Snake Eater or the open world of the Phantom Pain? Tell us in the comments. If you enjoyed this history, like the video and subscribe for more gaming history.
